chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn al-Fuḍayl wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام.

He asked him about a mamlūk whose master dies while he is away from him in another town, and in his hand is wealth belonging to his master. When al-Fiṭr arrives, should he pay zakat al-fiṭrah for himself from his master’s wealth, though it has now become the property of the orphans?

key_terms.الْفِطْرُ: the time of Eid al-Fiṭr when zakat al-fiṭrah becomes due
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكِ: an owned slave under the authority of a master
key_terms.الْيَتَامَى: the orphans who have inherited the estate
key_terms.مَالٌ: wealth or property held in possession

ai.seo_question: Should a slave pay zakat al-fiṭrah from his deceased master’s property that has passed to the orphans?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question addressed to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام concerning zakat al-fiṭrah in a case where a slave’s master has died and the estate has passed to orphans. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the slave should pay on his own behalf from the master’s wealth in his possession.
